newsitem.title: USA: Texas Auth. closer to defeasing Super Collider GOs.
newsitem.headline: Texas Auth. closer to defeasing Super Collider GOs.

text.p: After weighing several defeasance plans for roughly $200 million of general obligation debt outstanding for a Superconducting Super Collider project that never got off the ground, a Texas authority has narrowed its focus to just two, sources there said Thursday.

"I feel very comfortable that we have looked at all the options," a source at the Texas Public Finance Authority said, adding that she felt "very good" about the two remaining options being considered.

Back in 1989, Texas agreed to issue up to $1 billion of bonds to help construct the facility. In 1990 $250 million of general obligation bonds were issued, followed by a $250 million revenue bond deal in 1991, sources said.
When the U.S. goverment scrapped the project two or three years ago, it agreed to a monetary settlement with the state, they said.

"We used part of the federal settlement money to defease and extraordinarily redeem the $250 million worth of revenue bonds," another source said. In addition to the Federal money, TPFA used the revenue bond issue's unspent proceeds to help defease those bonds in 1996, the first source added.

The authority currently has $78 million in federal dollars left, plus some cash from asset sales, the sources said. TPFA plans to use that money to defease however much it can of the remaining GOs. Because some of those bonds began to mature as early as 1993, approximately $200 million GOs remain outstanding, they said.

Eight options had been on deck going into the TPFA board's February meeting, and that number had been winnowed to four when the board went into its meeting Wednesday. The board usually meets the third Wednesday of each month. The next meeting is set for April 16.
